name: six names for what it does, and the ticks must add up
one_line: Six names written for what something does, never for why, and twenty event-triggered glances whose ticks have to come to twenty.
how: Choose something that moves and does not depend on you: an animal, somebody cooking, the street from a window, the queue at a till. Watch five minutes writing nothing. Then write six names for things it does, under one rule — the name says what, never why. «Scratches its ear» is a name; «scratches because it itches» is not. The test is mechanical and gets printed: if the name contains a waits, a wants, a looks for or a because, rewrite it. The six must also be exclusive, so that at any instant exactly one holds. Then twenty glances, each triggered by something happening rather than by a clock, one tick each. Then add the ticks up.

knobs.knob: what a name is allowed to contain
knobs.effect: A name carrying a function can be wrong about the function: what looks like courtship may do something else entirely, and the same movement means opposite things in a cat and a dog. Describing the movement and nothing else is what lets a second person use the same list.

Sampling by the clock needs a clock and misses whatever is rare. Sampling by event — every time it moves, every time a car goes past — needs nothing at all, and is the only version available on paper.

knobs.knob: whether an arbitrary number may go inside a name
knobs.effect: «Licks the bars more than five times in thirty seconds» has no justification for the five and satisfies repeatability anyway, because the five is written down. A threshold that is declared is worth as much as a threshold that is right.

knobs.knob: whether the ticks are made to add up
knobs.effect: Twenty glances must give twenty ticks. More than twenty means two categories overlap; fewer means something happened that was not on the list, and the second is the most interesting thing the sheet produces.

where_the_work_is: In the arithmetic at the bottom. The total finds a fault in the grid rather than a mistake by whoever filled it in, and the two ways of being wrong have opposite signs, so the number says which fault it was.
breaks: The sheet cannot say what to observe, because it does not know where the reader is; the first line is where they declare it, and everything after works on whatever that was. Out of reach is agreement between observers, the stated reason the naming rules exist — and it costs nothing if a second person is around: hand them a copy and compare the two totals. Whoever counts finds what they expect, and the estimate is that observer bias can inflate an effect by a third to two thirds.
